questions.problem: Which of the following is the graph of the polar curve $\theta =\frac{3\pi }{8}?$
questions.worked_solution:
The polar curve defined by the equation $\theta =\frac{3\pi }{8}$ is the ray that starts at the origin and makes a counterclockwise angle of $\frac{3\pi }{8}$ with the positive $x$-axis. 

Therefore, the angle it makes with the negative $x$-axis is 

$$
\pi -\frac{3\pi }{8}=\frac{5\pi }{8}.
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Polar Equation of a Radial Line That Passes Through a Given Point
questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14040587/assets/19f94b8985a4b8da7899f984e0e1c3f88668aa59531658cd0118edb35aab1107.png)

Given that the ray above passes through the point with Cartesian coordinates $(-6,-2\sqrt{3})$, find the polar equation of the ray.
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find the reference angle associated with the point:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\theta }_{R} & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡|\frac{y}{x}| \\  & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡|\frac{-2\sqrt{3}}{-6}| \\  & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}) \\  & =\frac{\pi }{6}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, notice that the ray lies in the third quadrant. So, we find the angle in the third quadrant that has a reference angle ${\theta }_{R}=\frac{\pi }{6},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\theta  & =\pi +{\theta }_{R} \\  & =\pi +\frac{\pi }{6} \\  & =\frac{7\pi }{6}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the polar equation of the ray is 

$$
\theta =\frac{7\pi }{6}.
$$

questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14040587/assets/34b473c8e212297d8cb434fe0a2dd9872cfa2fda924ac3a4d528bc1318af8c5f.png)

The polar curve $r=8$ and the ray $\theta =\frac{5\pi }{6}$ intersect at the point $P,$ as shown above. What are the Cartesian coordinates of $P?$
questions.worked_solution:
The polar coordinates of $P$ are $(r,\theta )=(8,\frac{5\pi }{6}).$ We can convert the polar coordinates of $P$ to Cartesian coordinates, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\  & =8\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{5\pi }{6}) \\  & =8\cdot (-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}) \\  & =-4\sqrt{3} \\ y & =r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\  & =8\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{5\pi }{6}) \\  & =8\cdot (\frac{1}{2}) \\  & =4\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the Cartesian coordinates of $P$ are $(-4\sqrt{3},4).$

$$
